        - region "DIL content":
          - paragraph: Helping your child become a fluent reader at home is absolutely possible, and you don't need to be a trained teacher to do it. ❤️ The key is to make reading a little part of every day, teach the skills your child needs, and choose books that are challenging enough to help them grow without making them feel frustrated.
          - paragraph:
            - generic: Reading fluency means reading accurately, at a comfortable pace, and with expression while understanding what the words mean.
            - text: Reading quickly alone isn't the goal.
          - heading "1. Follow a simple 20-minute daily reading routine" [level=2]
          - paragraph: You can adapt this routine to your child's age and current reading level.
          - 'img "Managing Screen Time: Healthy Alternatives for Preschoolers"'
          - 'button "Open Managing Screen Time: Healthy Alternatives for Preschoolers"'
          - paragraph:
            - generic: 5 minutes — Read aloud to your child
          - paragraph: Choose an enjoyable story and read with expression. Let your child hear what smooth, meaningful reading sounds like. Talk about interesting words and pictures.
          - img "My First Phonics Kit - Best Preschools – BRAINIFY"
          - button "Open My First Phonics Kit - Best Preschools – BRAINIFY"
          - paragraph:
            - generic: 5 minutes — Practise sounds and words
          - paragraph:
            - text: Help your child connect letters to sounds, blend sounds into words, and recognise common words. For example, /s/ /u/ /n/ blends into
            - generic: sun
            - text: . Keep the practice short and playful.
          - img "Lecture et petite enfance | Fondation du Crédit Mutuel pour la lecture"
          - button "Open Lecture et petite enfance | Fondation du Crédit Mutuel pour la lecture"
          - paragraph:
            - generic: 5 minutes — Read together
          - paragraph: Take turns reading a sentence or paragraph. If your child struggles, model the sentence and invite them to read it again.
          - img "AI Literacy Learners | Grounded AI Literacy for K–12 Schools"
          - button "Open AI Literacy Learners | Grounded AI Literacy for K–12 Schools"
          - paragraph:
            - generic: 5 minutes — Talk about the story
          - paragraph: Ask questions such as “What happened?”, “Why did the character do that?” and “What do you think will happen next?”
          - paragraph: If your child is very young, start with 5–10 minutes. A happy, consistent habit is more useful than a long, stressful session.
          - heading "2. Use the “I read, we read, you read” method" [level=2]
          - paragraph:
            - text: This is one of the easiest ways to build confidence and fluency. Guided reading and rereading can improve word recognition, reading fluency and comprehension.
            - button "NICHD +1":
              - generic: NICHD
              - generic: "+1"

          - generic: Step 4

          - paragraph: Repeat the passage two or three more times if your child is comfortable. Aim for greater accuracy, smoother phrasing and expression—not just speed.

          - paragraph: For words that cannot be worked out easily using phonics, such as irregular words, explain the tricky part and practise recognising the word.
          - paragraph:
            - text: If your child repeatedly struggles with basic words, focus on explicit letter-sound instruction before asking them to read harder books. Systematic phonics, fluency practice, vocabulary and comprehension all play important roles in learning to read.

            - generic: Let your child choose
          - paragraph: Try comics, animal stories, jokes, poems or books about their favourite interests. Children are more likely to enjoy reading when the material interests them.
          - img "My Reading Buddy!"

          - paragraph:
            - generic: Create a reading audience
          - paragraph: Let your child read to a teddy bear, a sibling or another family member. This gives them a reason to practise.

          - paragraph:

          - paragraph: Find words beginning with the same sound, build words with letter cards, or hunt for familiar words on food packets and signs.
          - paragraph: "Praise specific improvements: “You sounded out that word all by yourself!” or “You paused at the full stop this time!” Avoid comparing your child with other children."
          - heading "5. Choose books at the right level" [level=2]
          - paragraph:
            - text: A useful reading book is one your child can read with reasonable accuracy while still learning something new. If nearly every sentence contains difficult words, choose an easier book for independent practice and read the harder book aloud together.
